name: Realtime voice conversation (OpenAI realtime or GPT-Live over WebRTC)
description: Low-latency, interruptible speech-to-speech: the phone streams audio straight to an OpenAI realtime voice model, which answers in a natural voice and hands anything that needs tools or memory to the person's agent. This is the upgrade path from VOX-01 when the turn-by-turn loop feels slow.
example: Hands full at the stove: Happy, how long do I rest a pork tenderloin... actually, first convert 425 Fahrenheit to a fan oven setting.
how:
`talk.realtime` block on the gateway: `provider` openai, a realtime model from the installed docs, `mode` realtime, `transport` webrtc (the iPhone path is client-owned WebRTC) and `brain` agent-consult so every tool call is routed through gateway policy on

-main. iOS client-owned WebRTC is Platform-key-only, so it needs an OpenAI Platform API key under `talk.realtime.providers.openai` (as a SecretRef), separate from the per-person chat provider ids. The host enforces a fresh spoken yes before high-impact actions started by voice. Finalized utterances are appended to the agent session so later text and voice turns share history.
depends_on: an OpenAI Platform key dedicated to voice
G004 spend caps extended to the voice key
decision: Zero Data Retention for the organisation that owns the voice key
caveats: Raw audio, not just text, goes to OpenAI for the whole call: with WebRTC the media runs directly between the device and the provider.

Billed separately from chat. OpenAI's pricing page lists gpt-live-1 at $0.05 per minute and gpt-realtime-mini at $10 in and $20 out per million audio tokens. Ten minutes a day on gpt-live-1 works out to about $15 a month per parent (my arithmetic). The price page says gpt-live-1 is billed per second and that backend model and tool usage are charged separately, so every agent-consult turn adds normal chat cost on top.
`talk.realtime` is one gateway-wide block, so the per-person provider ids and per-person cost split used for text do not carry over to voice.
The installed docs mark the iOS GPT-Live path as implemented with device live verification still pending, and GPT-Live sessions end at a 30-minute TTL.
In a kitchen with children talking in the background, their voices are streamed to a cloud model. Use it with the phone at the ear or headphones, or stay on VOX-01 push-to-talk.
For most kitchen questions the native loop is enough; realtime mainly buys barge-in and lower latency.

Retention: OpenAI's data-controls page lists the realtime endpoint with 30 days of abuse-monitoring retention unless the organisation has Zero Data Retention (the endpoint is eligible; GPT-Live sessions are listed separately and are also eligible). The M1 store-off decision covers chat calls through the custom provider ids and does not carry over to voice.
The per-minute GPT-Live price is not the whole bill: OpenAI's pricing page says backend model and tool usage are charged separately, so each agent-consult turn is billed again on the chat key.
The spoken confirmation gates the action, not the speaker: anyone in earshot, a child included, can say yes. It applies to voice-originated consult runs only.
Usable only on a phone that is already paired, which today means the operator's phone (see VOX-01).

Turning on `talk.realtime` is one gateway-wide choice for iPhone Talk: the docs say OpenAI realtime configs run as WebRTC on iOS and only non-realtime configs use the native loop. It is not a per-person upgrade from VOX-01; a per-device opt-in is documented for the Mac app only.
The default and the limited pairing codes both hand the phone operator.talk.secrets, the scope for reading Talk configuration with secrets included.
safety:
`brain: agent-consult` keeps tools behind the same

-main policy, hooks and approvals as text. The spoken-confirmation gate is host-enforced, bound to the final arguments and consumed once, so generated text cannot confirm on the user's behalf; it does not identify who spoke. The realtime voice model is a second cloud model outside

-main's provider policy: it hears the room and is given a bounded slice of the session's history. Headphones or phone-at-ear is a habit, not a control, so this stays out of shared rooms when children are present. Never point realtime at a kids agent: it is cloud audio by construction.
unverified: Whether a store:false style retention control applies to realtime sessions.
Whether realtime credentials can be set per agent or per person.
Real latency and barge-in quality on the home Wi-Fi.
Whether this OpenAI organisation has Zero Data Retention; without it realtime audio falls under the 30-day abuse-monitoring window.
What the 'bounded realtime profile context' sent to the voice provider contains for an agent that holds personal memory.
Whether an iPhone can stay on the native loop while `talk.realtime` is configured.
Whether Talk configuration read with operator.talk.secrets includes the realtime provider key.

name: Cooking companion by voice (hands-free kitchen session)
description: A parent props the phone on the counter and walks through a recipe by voice: next step, how much butter again, set a 12-minute reminder, with the ability to interrupt a long answer.
example: Happy, start the chili recipe I sent this morning, one step at a time.
how:
A workflow on

-main over VOX-01 (or VOX-02). The recipe arrives earlier as pasted text or a photo over iMessage (F001). A kitchen-mode section in AGENTS.md: one step per turn, short sentences, repeat quantities with units, no lists or links. `talk.interruptOnSpeech` gives barge-in; `talk.silenceTimeoutMs` is raised so a pause while stirring does not end the turn. Timers go through the existing reminders tool (F007) and arrive as a text.
caveats: For timers the phone or watch is simply better: a Siri timer is faster and audible, while Happy's reminder is an iMessage ping.
-main does not browse, so 'find me a recipe' is a research-agent job first (F019); the kitchen session works from text the parent chose to send.
With kids in the kitchen this should be push-to-talk on the parent's phone, not an open microphone.
The docs recommend headphones for open-microphone sessions because speaker audio feeds back into the mic.

The headphone advice in the docs is given for continuous realtime sessions, where the microphone stays open during playback; the turn-based native loop keeps echo suppression. It matters if this is run over VOX-02.
Inherits VOX-01: only the operator's phone can be paired within the family's separation rule today, so this is a one-parent workflow until that changes.
`talk.silenceTimeoutMs` is one gateway-wide key, so a longer pause for cooking slows every other Talk turn.
Voice Wake and background listening stay off in the kitchen: on iOS the recognizer may use Apple's network service, and children's speech would reach a cloud agent.
safety: Same agent, tool policy and hooks as typed chat; nothing new can leave the house through the agent, and the only content entering the memory-holding agent is the recipe the parent sent. The exposure is the room: other people's speech, children's included, is transcribed by Apple and answered by a cloud model, so the session is started and stopped by hand by the parent and never by wake word.
unverified: How well Apple dictation copes with extractor-fan and pan noise.
Whether the silence timeout can be changed per session rather than gateway-wide.
Whether the iPhone app has a user-facing hold-to-talk control; the docs list push-to-talk only as node commands.

name: Parent talks to Happy from the Apple Watch
description: Raise the wrist, ask, hear the answer. There are three ways and they differ a lot: dictating an ordinary iMessage to Happy from the Watch (works today), the OpenClaw Watch companion that relays one turn at a time through the iPhone, and a standalone realtime call placed by the Watch itself.
example: On a walk without the phone in hand: ask Happy whether the library is open tomorrow.
how: Path 1, nothing to build: Messages on the Watch to Happy's contact. Path 2, `Talk to Claw`: the OpenClaw Watch app (installed from the iPhone's Watch app) uses watchOS dictation, relays text through the paired iPhone app and reads the reply with the system voice; it needs the iPhone pairing from VOX-01 but no separate Watch pairing. Path 3, `Talk on Watch`: standalone realtime; setup gives the Watch its own node credential plus operator.read and operator.talk, audio is WebRTC Opus over UDP between the Watch and the provider, and it needs `talk.realtime` with webrtc transport plus a secure gateway URL that the Watch trusts and can reach by itself.
depends_on: VOX-01 phase 1 (operator's phone only) for the companion path
VOX-02 plus a non-tailnet gateway URL for the standalone path, which the inbound rule excludes
caveats: Standalone voice is effectively blocked here when away from the phone: the docs say a tailnet-only route is not enough, and this gateway is reachable only over Tailscale Serve.
The docs themselves say physical-Watch microphone and speaker routing, wrist-down use, network handoff, battery and long-call reliability still need device validation.
The Watch asks which agent to use, so it does not enforce one person, one agent.
Path 1 already covers the quick question from the wrist; the companion app adds a spoken reply, not a new ability.
Standalone setup requires the iPhone to be connected with operator.admin, the opposite of the reduced pairing in VOX-01 and VOX-03.
On the companion path the Watch also mirrors exec approval prompts from the iPhone with allow-once and deny buttons, which makes an approval one accidental tap away.
The Watch's own credential includes operator.read, which is not limited to one person's agent.
Standalone audio is WebRTC to the provider with no TURN or TCP fallback: cloud audio, and it fails on networks that block UDP.

Standalone setup needs the iPhone connected with operator.admin, so a phone paired with the limited code from VOX-03 cannot enrol the Watch. The companion path relays chat through the iPhone, so that phone needs the write scope.

The Watch transport needs a provider and authentication combination that supports gateway-controlled WebRTC and returns an ICE-lite answer with UDP candidates; there is no TURN relay and no TCP fallback.
safety: The Watch runs no agent; the gateway owns tools and policy. The companion path is only as safe as the iPhone pairing behind it, which today means the operator's phone. Standalone voice would need a certificate-trusted gateway URL reachable from outside the tailnet, which the Tailscale-only inbound rule forbids; do not open one for this. Plain Messages dictation to Happy adds no new credential and is the path to use.
unverified: Whether either adult owns an Apple Watch.
Apple's Watch Messages dictation page could not be fetched in this run, so path 1 rests on common knowledge rather than a cited page.

review_notes: Two of the three paths do not hold up for this install: the companion path inherits the VOX-01 phone pairing and mirrors approval prompts to the wrist, and standalone voice needs both an admin-scoped iPhone for setup and a gateway URL the Watch can reach outside the tailnet. Only plain Messages dictation is usable, and that path has no opened source.

All 6 sources hold. Path 1 is now sourced from Apple's Watch guide. Added that standalone Watch voice has to be set up from an iPhone holding operator.admin, which conflicts with the limited pairing in VOX-03, and the transport requirements the docs list.

name: Home Assistant Voice Preview Edition kitchen speaker
description: The roadmap's kitchen speaker: a small open device with a physical microphone mute where wake word, speech-to-text and text-to-speech can all run locally in Home Assistant, so only text would be handed to Happy. It is the only candidate with hardware mute and fully local speech, and its main purpose (kids) is blocked until there is a local model.
example: Okay Nabu, what is the weather this afternoon?
how: Buy the device. Run Home Assistant OS in a VM on the Mac (documented minimum 2 GB RAM and 2 vCPUs; a VirtualBox image for Apple Silicon, or UTM). Add Whisper or Speech-to-Phrase for speech-to-text and Piper for speech through the Wyoming integration for a fully local pipeline. Then a conversation agent must forward the text to a stateless OpenClaw agent, and that hop is the unsolved part: Home Assistant's official OpenAI integration only talks to OpenAI's own endpoint, and OpenClaw's OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint (off by default; the config repo's flat config has it enabled on this gateway) is documented as full operator access. With token auth a bearer token gets the full operator scope set and the request's model field chooses the agent, so Home Assistant would hold an owner-level credential that can reach any agent unless a small kids-only shim sits in between, as the roadmap already notes.
depends_on: Home Assistant OS VM on the Mac
a scoped endpoint or shim between Home Assistant and the gateway
caveats: The price on Home Assistant's page is now $69 (59 EUR); the roadmap says $59.
Home Assistant itself calls it a preview that cannot yet do everything commercial assistants do.
It adds an always-on VM to patch and back up, in a house whose only Home Assistant relevant gear is Hue, Sonos and one TV.
Open-ended questions need Whisper, which Home Assistant recommends only on powerful hardware; the fast Speech-to-Phrase option covers home-control phrases only.

Without a local model, a speaker question reaches OpenAI as text. A room speaker cannot be made adults-only, because nothing identifies who is speaking, so there is no interim adult version: the device stays blocked until a local model exists.
Side benefit if it is ever built: Home Assistant's Sonos integration gives the announce feature in VOX-07 for free.

Home Assistant's OpenAI page points to its OpenRouter integration for other providers and offers no custom base URL, so the bridge would be a community integration or a self-written shim (not verified which).
safety: Speech stays inside the house. The risk is the bridge credential: the chat-completions endpoint is equivalent to an operator secret. The speaker must reach only a tool-less, memory-less agent, and kids' questions may only go to a local model with the roadmap's classifiers in front.
unverified: Which Home Assistant conversation integration can target a custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint in 2026 (the roadmap cites a community one; I did not verify it).
Whisper latency inside a VM on this Mac.
Whether OpenClaw can issue an HTTP credential scoped to one agent.

Whether a trusted-proxy identity in front of the HTTP endpoint could narrow a caller to one agent. With the token auth this gateway uses, the docs say scope headers are ignored and the request's model field selects any agent.

name: Bundled device skills: what each one controls and how it signs in
description: A decision record for the nine bundled skills in this lens. Two fit the house (openhue, sonoscli), one belongs to research (goplaces), one is already beaten by the in-house weather plugin, and five do not apply or should be skipped. All of them are instructions for running a command-line tool, so on this stack (no exec for any agent) each is reference material for a host-side plugin, not something to switch on.
example: Operator question: which of the bundled home skills do we install?
how: openhue: Hue Bridge on the LAN, lights, rooms and scenes only; pairing by pressing the bridge button once, after which a local app key sits in ~/.openhue/config.yaml. sonoscli: local UPnP/SOAP to each speaker on port 1400, no account; discovery needs the macOS Local Network permission for the Gateway's parent process. camsnap: RTSP/ONVIF cameras with a user and password in ~/.config/camsnap/config.yaml, plus local webcams on macOS; needs ffmpeg. eightctl: Eight Sleep account email and password against an unofficial, rate-limited API. spotify-player: Spotify Premium, with spogo importing browser cookies. blucli: Bluesound/NAD players only. songsee: turns an audio file into spectrogram images, not a home control. weather: wttr.in through web_fetch or curl, no key, and it defers to official services for severe alerts. goplaces: Google Places text search and details with GOOGLE_PLACES_API_KEY. Keep openhue and sonoscli as backends for the F076/F077 plugins in the home agent; leave the rest uninstalled.
caveats: Every skill assumes the agent can run shell commands; Happy's agents cannot, so nothing here works by enabling a skill alone.
eightctl and spotify-player hand an agent a full account login (password or browser cookies) for a convenience the vendor apps already give; skip both.
The house has no Bluesound, Eight Sleep or RTSP camera, so blucli, eightctl and the network-camera half of camsnap have nothing to talk to.
The bundled weather skill uses wttr.in; the in-house home_weather plugin on api.weather.gov is the better source for alerts.
safety: No new grant is made by this entry. The two skills kept are wrapped by plugins with allowlists and caps in code and live only in the stateless home agent.
unverified: Whether spogo's cookie import can be scoped to one browser profile; not checked because the skill is not recommended.

name: LG TV: off at bedtime, notice on screen
description: Turn the TV off by text or at a set time on school nights, lower the volume, and optionally show a short notice on screen first. This adds a second route to F078's HomeKit Shortcut: Home Assistant's LG webOS integration, which can also put a message on the TV.
example: 20:30 on school nights: the TV shows 'TV off in 10 minutes', then switches off.
how: Route A: an allowlisted Shortcut named 'TV off' in happy's account, run with the shortcuts command by the F078 plugin; happy's Apple Account must be a member of the Home, and a member without remote control can act only while at home on the home network, which is where the Mac mini sits. Route A can switch the TV off but cannot show a message. Route B (needs HOM-01): Home Assistant's webOS media player turns the TV off or changes volume, and the on-screen line is the per-TV notify action. Because the MCP server works through Assist intents, put 'show notice N, wait, turn off' into one Home Assistant script whose only field picks from fixed strings, and expose that script. Power-on is left out. Scheduled runs are command or home-agent jobs with a skip-tonight file, as in F081.
caveats: The TV is the only HomeKit accessory in the house, so this is the whole of 'HomeKit control' today.
Apple Home can already switch an accessory off at a time of day, but automations need a home hub (HomePod or Apple TV), which is not in the inventory.
The webOS integration cannot power the TV on by itself (it needs Wake-on-LAN) and requires the TV's 'LG Connect Apps' setting.
Because a HomeKit accessory pairs with one controller, the Home Assistant route uses LG's own network API, not HomeKit.
The remote on the sofa is still the fastest off switch; the value is the scheduled, argument-free cut-off.
The cut-off is advisory: nothing stops a child from pressing power on the remote a minute later.
On most newer TV firmware the notice shows text only, and passing an icon can stop it from appearing.
The on-screen notice is available only through Home Assistant (Route B); the HomeKit Shortcut route can only switch the TV off or change what HomeKit exposes.
safety: Low-consequence actuation with a name allowlist; on-screen text is picked from fixed strings so nothing from the web or from a model's free text reaches the screen. The home agent has no memory or web tool.
unverified: Whether the house has an Apple home hub.
The TV's webOS version and whether on-screen notifications work on its firmware.

Whether a HomeKit action in a Shortcut run on the Mac mini works for the non-admin happy user, and whether happy's Apple Account can be added to the Home without a home hub; Apple's hub page lists sharing among the things a hub enables, while its sharing page does not mention a hub.
Whether the TV's own power-off timer already covers a fixed nightly cut-off; LG's support page did not render in this run.
Whether scripts exposed to Assist are offered as tools by Home Assistant's MCP server (same open point as HOM-03).

name: Sonos announce (intercom-style)
description: A parent texts an announcement and the house speakers say it, then go back to what they were playing. The 9 Oct catalog parks this as a later toy under F077; this entry spells out the two real ways to do it and what each costs.
example: Happy, tell the house the bus leaves in ten minutes.
how:
Trigger is deterministic, not a model decision: a `before_dispatch` claim on a fixed prefix such as `announce:` from an adult's handle hands the parent's words verbatim to the tool, so

-main (which reads search results) never decides to speak to the house and no cloud-written text is played to the children. If an agent tool form is kept, each announcement needs an approval. The tool itself, `announce(text, rooms)`, lives in the planned `home-sonos` plugin. It synthesizes the text with the local engine from VOX-04, serves the file from a small HTTP server bound to the LAN address only (one directory, short-lived random file names, inbound firewall exception for the speakers), and plays it. Route A, no Home Assistant: the Sonos audio-clip command `loadAudioClip` with a `streamUrl`, which mixes the clip with whatever is playing but is documented under the cloud Control API with OAuth and an API key; or sonoscli `play-uri`, which replaces what is playing and restores nothing. Route B, if Home Assistant is ever installed for VOX-11: its Sonos integration plays an announcement with `announce: true` and restores the volume. In code: text length cap, volume cap, quiet hours from G001, speaker allowlist, a daily cap.
depends_on: decision: Sonos account OAuth, Home Assistant, or local play-uri only
caveats: The bundled sonoscli skill documents discover, status, play, volume and grouping only; it has no announce or speech command. The tool's site lists `play-url` and `play-uri`, but I could not confirm that either resumes the previous music.
Sonos audio clips only work on players that report the AUDIO_CLIP capability; the two speakers here are unchecked.
LAN speaker control from the gateway needs the macOS Local Network permission for the launchd node process.
A talking house at the wrong moment is worse than no feature; quiet hours and a low daily cap matter more than voice quality.

The overlay is unverified without Home Assistant. Sonos documents loadAudioClip under its cloud Control API (OAuth scope plus API key), and Home Assistant's page says its announcements need TCP port 1443 open on each speaker, which suggests a local interface exists; Sonos' own page does not document one.
Home Assistant's page warns that older hardware and S1 firmware may not fully support announcements.
The 9 Oct scan found the two speakers in the living room and the family room, so an announcement does not reach the kitchen or bedrooms.
The clip server would be the first LAN-facing listener on the gateway Mac.
The Sonos cloud route puts a Sonos account token on the gateway and makes a house announcement depend on an internet round trip.

The speaker has to fetch the clip from the Mac over HTTP, so this adds a LAN-facing listener to a host whose gateway binds only to loopback today. It should serve nothing but the generated clip files and be covered by the host firewall review.

Sonos accepts only MP3 or WAV clips (the local engines emit WAV, which fits). Home Assistant notes that announcements need TCP port 1443 reachable on each speaker and may not work on older S1 hardware.
The `sonos` binary is not installed; the bundled skill installs it with `go install`, so a Go toolchain is a prerequisite.
safety:
The audience is everyone in the house, guests and children included, so this is an outbound channel in its own right even though nothing leaves the building. It must not be callable by an agent that reads untrusted content without an approval:

-main reads search and research results, so the safe trigger is a fixed prefix claimed before the model, speaking the parent's words verbatim. Never reachable from research or mail readers. Speech is synthesized locally, with the VOX-04 hardening in place. Text length, volume, quiet hours, speaker allowlist and a daily cap are enforced in code. No lock, alarm or door is involved.
unverified: Whether sonoscli `play-uri` restores the prior queue or stream after a clip.
Whether these two Sonos models support audio clips, and whether a purely local clip endpoint is usable without the Sonos cloud.
Latency from text to sound.
Whether the Sonos Control API route needs a registered developer integration (client id and secret) before OAuth works.

That makes it experimental rather than a straightforward build, and the clip server is a new LAN listener.

name: Home Assistant as the house hub, reached over MCP
description: OpenClaw 2026.9.7 has no Home Assistant, HomeKit, Matter or MQTT integration of its own (none in the docs, none among the bundled plugins). The official route is Home Assistant's MCP Server integration: one endpoint through which a stateless home agent reads state and controls only the entities a parent has exposed, covering Hue, Sonos and the LG TV with one audited list instead of one plugin per brand.
example: Are any lights or the TV still on downstairs?
how: Run Home Assistant OS in a VM on the Mac mini (the roadmap already plans this VM for the kids' speaker). Add the Hue, Sonos and LG webOS integrations, then the 'Model Context Protocol Server' integration; turn off 'Expose all LLM APIs' and expose only the wanted entities. In OpenClaw add mcp.servers.<name> with url http://<ha-host>:8123/api/mcp, transport 'streamable-http' written out (when it is omitted OpenClaw uses sse), and the Home Assistant long-lived token in headers.Authorization, supplied through a secret reference and not a config literal (auth 'oauth' with openclaw mcp login is the documented alternative). This Gateway uses tools.profile 'minimal', which hides MCP tools, so grant them only to the stateless 'home' agent from F076 by listing the <server>__<tool> names in that agent's alsoAllow and in its sandbox tool allow list (tools.sandbox.tools.alsoAllow); no other agent then sees the server. Write toolFilter.include after a live probe (openclaw mcp doctor <name> --probe), since it selects tools by name. The registry before_tool_call hook stays as the second, fail-closed gate and enforces quiet hours.
depends_on: Home Assistant OS VM (2 GB RAM, 2 vCPU, bridged network adapter)
egress proxy exception for the Home Assistant LAN address
decision: direct CLIs (F076/F077) or Home Assistant as the single device path, not both
caveats: Home Assistant's MCP option 'Expose all LLM APIs' is on by default and the token belongs to an administrator account by default; both need tightening before OpenClaw connects.
The MCP server does not support notifications or sampling, so Home Assistant cannot push a state change to Happy through MCP; events need a separate webhook (see HOM-06).
A HomeKit accessory can pair with only one controller, so the LG TV stays in Apple Home and joins Home Assistant through the webOS integration, not through HomeKit.
Home Assistant's macOS install page recommends dedicated hardware unless a hypervisor is already in use; it is one more service to patch and back up.
Running both the direct CLIs and Home Assistant doubles the paths to the same lamp; pick one.
With only Hue, two Sonos and one TV today, the hub pays off mainly if presence (HOM-05), announcements (HOM-03) or the kids' speaker are also wanted.

Home Assistant's macOS page documents VirtualBox (UTM only as a fallback for people used to virtual machines) and points anyone not comfortable with virtual machines to a dedicated board; the VM is one more service to patch, back up and bring back after every reboot and FileVault unlock, and until it is up every home tool fails.

Home Assistant's MCP server offers its Assist intents plus any scripts exposed to Assist, not arbitrary actions; anything beyond on/off, brightness, volume and state reads (announcements, TV notices) needs a script a parent writes and exposes.

Because those tools are generic intents, toolFilter.include narrows verbs, not device classes; the exposure list in Home Assistant and a before_tool_call check on each call's target are the real limits.

The long-lived token is a ten-year credential for Home Assistant's APIs as one user; the exposed-entity limit applies to the MCP tools, not to the token, so it must stay host-side and be rotated by hand.
State text returned by Home Assistant (now-playing titles, device names) is third-party text read by an agent that can actuate; allowlists and caps in code have to bound the result.

Home Assistant's MCP options 'Expose all LLM APIs' and 'Require an administrator account' are both on by default: out of the box every LLM API is offered and the token must belong to an administrator. Tighten the first before OpenClaw connects; a token for a non-admin Home Assistant user works only after the second is turned off.

Home Assistant's macOS page is written for people who already run a supported hypervisor (VirtualBox, with UTM as the fallback) and points everyone else to a dedicated board; the VM is one more service to patch and back up.

toolFilter selects MCP tools by name, not by device. Home Assistant's LLM API works through intents, so one tool may act on any exposed entity; the per-device limit lives in Home Assistant's exposure list and in the hook, not in toolFilter.
Home Assistant exposes new entities in the cover domain (garage doors and gates) to Assist by default, so the exposure list needs a review after each device is added (see HOM-12).
safety: The home agent keeps no memory, has no web tool and no outbound message tool, so it holds no private data and cannot send anything out; the only outside text it reads is device state. Only exposed entities are reachable through MCP; locks, garage, alarm, gate and cameras are never exposed in Home Assistant, and a fail-closed hook that inspects each call's target repeats that block on the OpenClaw side (HOM-12). The token is a wider credential than the MCP tools and is kept host-side only.
unverified: Whether Home Assistant OS runs cleanly under VirtualBox or UTM on macOS 27 with an M5 chip.
Whether openclaw mcp login completes against Home Assistant's OAuth; both sides document OAuth but the pair was not tried, so the long-lived token path is assumed.
The exact tool names Home Assistant's MCP server exposes (not listed on the page fetched), so the toolFilter list must be written after a live probe.
Whether the Smokescreen egress proxy applies to MCP HTTP calls to a LAN address.
Whether a non-administrator Home Assistant user can use the MCP endpoint once 'Require an administrator account' is turned off, and what that user can still reach.
Whether a Home Assistant long-lived token is confined to the MCP endpoint or carries its owner's full API rights; the authentication page fetched does not say.
Which macOS account runs the VM and how it comes back headless after a reboot (FileVault needs a manual unlock).

name: Is anyone home? (house-level presence)
description: A who-is-home answer for parents and a condition for other jobs, such as lights left on with nobody in the house. OpenClaw's own presence tool and geolocation plugin do not answer this: they describe clients connected to the Gateway and turn a public IP into a rough city, which returns nothing on a tailnet or LAN.
how: Home Assistant Companion app on each adult's iPhone creates a device tracker; a person entity per adult follows it; the home zone's state is the number of people inside. Set the app's location reporting to 'Zone Name Only' so coordinates stay on the phone. The home agent reads the zone and person states through the MCP server (HOM-01); these entity types are not exposed to Assist by default and have to be exposed by hand. Each phone needs a path to Home Assistant when it is away (Tailscale to the VM), because a leave report is sent after the phone has left the home Wi-Fi. Without Home Assistant, the lighter option is a Shortcuts automation on each adult's iPhone (Arrive, Leave or Wi-Fi) that posts to a mapped Gateway hook as in HOM-06, with a small state file as the house-level signal; it is no more accurate than the phone's own geofence.
depends_on: Home Assistant Companion app on both adults' iPhones

both phones able to reach Home Assistant away from home (Tailscale on each phone and Home Assistant on the tailnet); Home Assistant listens only on the local network by default and the roadmap rules out port forwarding
a path from the phones to Home Assistant when away (Tailscale)
caveats: The iOS app's cheapest location updates are the least accurate kind and can lag, so 'just left' may be a few minutes stale.
The kids have no phones, so 'anyone' means the two adults.
Watching for phones on Wi-Fi is brittle: iPhones present a private Wi-Fi address per network, with a rotating option, and sleep.
Apple Home tracks arrival and departure for its own automations but a Mac cannot trigger a location automation, and Happy cannot read that state.
The presence tool reports people as online when a client is connected, including idle tabs, which is unrelated to being at home.

Watching for phones on Wi-Fi is brittle mainly because phones sleep and drop off the network; on a WPA2 or WPA3 home network the iPhone's private address is fixed by default and rotates only if set to Rotating or on weakly secured networks.
The count covers the two adults only. With the kids at home with a sitter or a grandparent it reads zero, so it must never be the only condition for switching anything off.
A departure is recorded only if the phone can reach Home Assistant from outside the house; with a LAN-only server and no VPN up, the house keeps showing that adult as home.
The Companion app sends location straight to the family's own Home Assistant, or through Home Assistant Cloud if that service is switched on; leave Cloud off so presence stays in the house.
safety: Presence is private data. Phones report zone names only. Only the count of people in the home zone is exposed to the home agent; per-person zones are one person's data and stay unexposed, so one adult's agent cannot read the other's whereabouts (roadmap section 1b). The count is never available to the research agent or a kids agent.
unverified: That Apple offers no programmatic way to read Home or Find My presence (a negative that could not be sourced).
The exact iOS location permission level the Companion app needs; the page fetched does not state it.
Whether the Companion app queues or drops a zone change when the server is unreachable; the location page does not say.
Whether a zone entity can be exposed to Assist on its own; if not, a helper sensor holding the count is needed.
Whether person and zone entities, once exposed, are returned by the MCP server's tools; the default exposed domains in Home Assistant's source do not include person, zone or device_tracker.

name: Multi-day family project with check-ins
description: A parent hands Happy a project with an end date (birthday party, weekend trip, garage clean-out). Happy keeps one project note with decisions and open items, checks in on a schedule it paces itself, runs research legs in the background, and stops when the date passes. New against the 9 Oct catalog: durable project state plus paced check-ins; F028 only covers a one-shot plan.
example: Plan our 10-year-old's birthday party for Saturday the 14th: 10 kids, indoor, under 300 dollars. Check in with me every few days until it is sorted.
how:
Held by the asking parent's

-main. State: one project note (memory/projects/.md through the F041 write path, or home-store rows from F031) with goal, end date, decisions, open items and a review date. The note records only what the parent typed or confirmed, written in a turn that carried no web or research results. Check-ins: one isolated automation per project, created through the `automations` tool on

-main with a `pacing` object (`min`, `max`; `--pacing-min` and `--pacing-max` are the CLI spelling), so each run can call `automations(action: "next_check")` and be clamped to those bounds. The job's tool cap holds the note or home-store read tools plus `automations` (inside an automation run that tool is limited to the run's own job) and never `sessions_spawn` or a web tool; announce to the owner; NO_REPLY when nothing is due; the run removes its own job after the end date. Hard prerequisites before `automations` is allowed on

-main: the fail-closed before_tool_call pin must also match `automations`/`cron` add and update and refuse webhook delivery, completion and failure destinations, and any recipient other than the asking parent; and `cron.triggers.enabled: false`, so the tool does not offer script payloads, trigger scripts or stream commands. Research legs: `sessions_spawn` to the stateless `research` agent with `runTimeoutSeconds` and `completionTarget: "parent"`, in interactive turns only, so

-main reviews the result privately before it texts anything. Decisions are plain proposals in chat (or `ask_user` while the parent is in the conversation). `/goal` is not the durable state here (see AUT-02).
depends_on: F041 memory write path or F031 home-store
decision: Jordan as a command owner
delivery pin hook that covers automations/cron add and update (extends G009 and F007)
caveats: Scheduled runs do not get MEMORY.md injected, so a check-in must read the project note with a tool or carry the state in the job message.
A job created from chat is capped to the tools the creating turn had and cannot be widened later, so a check-in can never do more than the parent's own main agent.
The conversation resets every morning at 04:00 and that also wipes any /goal; the project note is the only continuity between days.
Every check-in is a cloud model turn. Pace in days, not minutes, and cap active projects per person (three is plenty).

Published measurements put the reliable autonomous working span of frontier models at well under a working day, so the design is many short runs with a parent between them, not one long unattended run.
No bookings, purchases or invitations sent: the output is options, links and drafts. A static checklist is still easier in a shared Notes or Reminders list; Happy adds the nudging and the research.

The one long-task measurement opened in this run dates from March 2025 and covers software tasks: the frontier model of that time finished about half of the tasks that take a person roughly 50 minutes. It says nothing direct about gpt-6-sol or about family planning. The case for many short runs with a parent between them rests on cost and on keeping a person in the loop, not on that number.

Command-owner status is gateway-wide: an owner can ask their agent to list, inspect, update, run or remove any job on the gateway, whoever created it. Once Jordan is an owner, each parent's agent can read and change the other's check-in jobs, so job messages must not carry private detail.

The F041 plan refuses memory writes in a turn tainted by web results, and a turn that received a research result is tainted. Research findings therefore cannot be saved into the project note in that turn: they stay in the chat thread, and the note holds only what the parent states or confirms afterwards.
safety:
-main holds the note and never browses; `research` does every web leg, has no memory, and as a sub-agent can never get the message, cron or gateway tools. The `automations` tool is itself a send path: a job can name any chat as its delivery target or post its result to a webhook URL.

-main holds memory and reads search snippets, so the recipient pin must cover `automations`/`cron` calls, not only `message`, and must refuse webhook mode before the tool is granted. Check-in runs carry no web tool and no `sessions_spawn`; that is the hard limit. The rule that handoff text carries dates, ages and budget only (never names, school or address) is prompt text, not enforcement. With the pin in place nothing on the never list is reachable: there is no payment, booking or outbound-to-strangers tool anywhere in the chain.

review_notes: All nine sources check out, but the safety case has a hole: the `automations` tool this feature depends on can set a job's delivery to any chat or to a webhook URL, and command-owner status lets either parent's agent read and edit the other's jobs. The project note also collides with the F041 rule that tainted turns cannot write memory. Value lowered to 3.

name: Self-paced watch loop (/loop and paced automations)
description: "Keep checking this until it happens, then tell me": a recurring agent turn bound to the conversation, at a fixed interval or self-paced so it checks more often while things move and backs off when quiet.
example: /loop 30m has the district posted a decision about tomorrow's snow day? Stop once it is posted.
how:
`/loop [interval] ` typed to

-main makes the agent create a recurring agent-turn job in that conversation through the `automations` tool; with no interval it self-paces between 1 minute and 1 hour using `next_check`. `/loop status` and `/loop stop` manage it. Longer-lived watchers are created by happy-deploy with `openclaw automations add --pacing-min ... --pacing-max ...` and an explicit `--tools` cap. Needs `automations` allowed on

-main (it is denied today with the rest of `group:automation`).
depends_on: decision: Jordan as a command owner
F029 for anything that needs page content
delivery pin hook that covers automations/cron add and update (extends G009 and F007)
caveats: Owner-only: Jordan cannot use /loop unless she is listed as a command owner, which is a gateway-wide elevation. An owner can list, inspect, update, run or remove every job on the gateway, including the other parent's.
Every tick is a cloud model turn and the self-paced floor is one minute. Require an explicit interval of 15 minutes or more and a stop condition, in AGENTS.md.

-main has web_search only, so a loop sees search snippets, not page content. Whether a change posted minutes ago shows up in snippets within the loop interval is untested, so the snow-day example is not dependable this way. Real page watching belongs to the research agent (F029).
A loop does not end by itself. The scheduler disables a recurring job only after 10 failures in a row, so the prompt must say when to stop.
Nothing fires while the Mac is off or locked after a reboot.
For known sources the phone is already better: district push alerts, carrier tracking, calendar alerts.
safety:
Inside a loop run the `automations` tool is limited to the run's own job, and the result returns to the conversation that created it. The exposure comes from granting `automations` to

-main at all: in an interactive owner turn the tool can create a job whose delivery names any chat or a webhook URL and, unless `cron.triggers.enabled` is false, script payloads, trigger scripts and stream commands.

-main holds memory and reads untrusted search snippets, so without a fail-closed before_tool_call pin on `automations`/`cron` that refuses webhook mode and any recipient but the asker, the tool completes the trifecta. With the pin in place and triggers off, what remains is the exposure

-main already has with web_search, now repeated unattended. Keep loops short-lived, count them against the G001 daily cap, and never give a looped agent web_fetch.
